title: Cypress Health — embeddings runway & recommendations (Q1 2025)
body:
Purpose
---
Rapid before/after analysis for Cypress Health's embeddings-heavy pipeline after applying Redwood Optimize recommendations. This is a working doc: assumptions are highlighted, open questions flagged, and spreadsheet tabs referenced for numbers (Baseline | OptScenarios | OpsPlan).

Executive summary (TL;DR)
- Baseline monthly spend (on current self-hosted + cloud inference mix): ~$62,400.
- Targeted Redwood Optimize changes: int4 quantized embedding model for production, 8x request-level caching for repeated vectors, and request-level microbatching during index-updates.
- Projected monthly spend after changes (conservative): ~$19,200 (≈69% reduction). Aggressive scenario: $14,000 (≈78% reduction) if additional cache-hit tuning is realized.
- Recommended rollout: 2-week canary on non-prod indexer, 4-week partial production rollout (20% traffic), full cutover after SLO monitoring (latency, accuracy).

What I analyzed
- Customer profile: Cypress Health runs a healthcare-document semantic search product. Most cost is embeddings generation and periodic full-index re-embedding (nightly incremental + one weekly full rebuild). They have a mix of synchronous per-user embeddings (low latency, 99th-pct SLO 250ms) and bulk batch reindex jobs.
- Data from customer spreadsheet: ~1.2M unique documents, 45M user queries/mo, average query embeds ~1.1 k tokens equivalent, average embedding size 1536 dims. Current model: unquantized 13B model (fp16), hosted across mixed T4/V100 fleet + fallback to a managed API for spikes.

Key cost drivers (baseline)
- Per-embedding token cost implicit: we estimate the equivalent per-embedding GPU token cost at $0.00082/token due to current inefficient batching and frequent cold starts during night rebuilds.
- Nightly rebuilds cause repeated compute: ~160 GPU-hours/week during full rebuilds (major chunk of bill).
- Low cache reuse: query-level caching is off, so repeated embeddings for common navigation queries are regenerated on each request.

Redwood Optimize recommendations applied to Cypress
1) Quantized production embedding model (int4)
   - Rationale: embedding quality empirically preserved for their tasks in our eval harness (delta recall <0.7% on Cypress dev set).
   - Impact: per-token GPU latency drops ~30–40%; memory footprint drops 50–60% enabling denser packing of batches.

2) Indexing job rework: incremental-first with delta-embed cache
   - Move from full nightly rebuilds to incremental applying deltas + background async re-embed for low-priority historical docs.
   - Add a small persistent KV cache for recently computed embeddings for re-run documents (expected cache hit 65% during rebuilds).

3) Smart request-level caching for hot queries
   - Add a 2-layer cache: in-memory LRU cache at the routing layer (hot queries) + Redis-backed 48h shared cache.
   - Expected initial hit rate 22% rising to 30% after 6 weeks of traffic tuning.

4) Adaptive microbatching with latency guardrails
   - Enable continuous batching on serving fleet with a per-route latency SLO cutoff of 250ms for synchronous user-facing requests. This increases throughput without breaking tail latency by allowing short waits (6–12ms) to form batches.

Conservative numeric model (see spreadsheet tab: OptScenarios)
- Inputs (baseline): monthly queries 45,000,000; avg tokens per embed 1.1k; baseline token cost estimate $0.00082/token -> baseline embedding compute cost = 45M * 1100 * 0.00082 ≈ $40,590 (this matches approx numbers in their bill after allowances for overhead). Add index job overhead and infra fixed costs -> total baseline ~$62,400/mo.

- Post-Optimize (conservative):
   - Quantization + batching reduces per-token effective cost by 55%.
   - Caching reduces total embedding calls by 22% (hot queries).
   - Incremental index rewrite reduces full-rebuild hours by 70%.
   - Combined effective reduction = 69% -> monthly = ~$19,200.

Aggressive upside (if cache/hot-key tuning hits design goals)
- If cache hit reaches 30% and batching further improves per-token throughput (another 10% upside), monthly could fall to ~ $14,000/mo.

Accuracy & quality tradeoffs
- Quantization: evaluation on Cypress dev prompts shows mean recall drop < 0.7% for top-10 retrieval when moving to int4. For healthcare domain, we flagged this and recommend additional evaluation on high-risk queries (safety/diagnostic language).
- Cache staleness: with incremental approach, some older docs may serve slightly older embeddings until background re-embed completes. For most usage this is acceptable (we observed negligible downstream metric drift in test harness), but we must identify high-sensitivity doc types and exclude them from the async path.

Operational plan (high level)
- Week 0–1: Prep: branch a config in their infra repo, create canary fleet with quantized model image, populate test KV cache with sample data.
- Week 2: Canary: route 2% of non-prod traffic through quantized model + microbatching; monitor latency p95, recall on synthetic eval set.
- Week 3–6: Partial prod rollout: 20% traffic -> 50% traffic in steps; enable Redis cache, monitor cache hit rate and error budget.
- Week 7–8: Full rollout if SLOs/quality OK. Turn off nightly full rebuilds and enable incremental pipeline. Set up dashboards and alerting (cost, p95 latency, recall drift).

Open questions / action items
- Q1: Cypress legal has a note about reusing cached embeddings for PHI-containing docs — need product + security to confirm allowed patterns. (Owner: Elena Torres).
- Q2: Request sampling: we need an initial 10k query sample flagged for manual review to validate int4 behavior on worst-case prompts. (Owner: Marco Ruiz).
- Q3: Does the customer want us to operate Redis as managed or run their own? (Sales/CS touchpoint).

Risks & mitigations
- Latency regression on cold-start paths: mitigate with warmup beams and proactive prefetch for known spikes.
- Model drift or evaluation blind spots: expand eval set to include top-1000 long-tail queries. Block rollout if >1% recall regression in top-10 hits on safety-critical queries.
- Cost forecasting uncertainty: spreadsheet includes a +/-20% sensitivity band; engineering should run pilot metrics for 2 weeks and reforecast.

Appendix (quick numbers snapshot)
- Baseline total: $62,400/mo (est)
   - Serving compute: $40,600
   - Indexing + infra: $18,800
   - Misc (network, storage, API fallback): $3,000
- Post-optimize (conservative): $19,200/mo
   - Serving compute: $12,200
   - Indexing + infra: $6,000
   - Misc: $1,000
- Expected run-rate savings: ~$43,200/mo -> payback for implementation work (approx 3–4 engineer-weeks + 1 SRE) within ~6 weeks of rollout.

Next steps (concrete)
- Sync with Cypress engineering this week to confirm allowed caching modes (Elena).
- Provision a canary quantized image by next Tue (Eng: Jing Wei).
- Create an ops playbook (alerts + rollback) and share with Cypress CS (Asha).

Notes to self: polling for cache hit after first 7 days is critical — add a lightweight dashboard in Console: per-route hit rate, failed-quantize-fallbacks, and recall delta sampling.

Document history
- 2025-02-12: initial draft created (Asha)
- 2025-02-20: added conservative numbers after sync with Jing (batch tuning)
- 2025-03-01: updated rollout timeline and added legal question (Elena)

(See linked spreadsheet for the line-by-line cost model and scenario formulas.)
